chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who was a close relative to me, who died and left young children, and left owned slave boys and girls, and he had not bequeathed. So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, taking her as a mother of a child (of his), and what is your view regarding selling them? He said: 'If there is a guardian for them who manages their affairs, sells on their behalf, and looks out for their interests, he is rewarded in doing so.' I said: 'So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, taking her as a mother of a child?' He said: 'There is no problem with that. When the custodian sells on their behalf, being considerate of their interests regarding what is beneficial for them, it is not for them to retract regarding what the custodian has done for them, being considerate of their interests regarding what is beneficial for them.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (a female slave who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling slave children left by a deceased relative without a will?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the validity of selling minor slaves when a guardian acts in their best interest, ensuring the transaction is binding even if the girl later becomes an 'Umm al-Walad'. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the guardian's discretion for the minors' welfare precludes their later right to contest the sale, reflecting the practical management of property and status in early Islamic society.

en.hubeali: A number of our companion, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra’ib who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> about a man who was a close relative, died and left young children, and left owned slave boys and girls, and he had not bequeathed. So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding the one who buys the slave girls from them. Can he take her as a mother for (his) children, and what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding selling them?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there was a guardian for them who would stand with their affairs, selling upon them, and looking out for them, and he would be Recompensed with regards to them’.
I said, ‘So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, so he takes her as a mother of a child (of his)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that. When the custodian sells upon them being considerate for them regarding what is correct for them, so it is not for them that they should retract regarding what the custodian has done for them, having been considerate for them regarding what is correct for them’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who is of my relatives who has left behind small children, slave-boys and slave-girls, and has not made any will. ‘What do you say about one who buys from them a slave-girl for a mother of one’s child and what do you say about selling them?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If they have a guardian he looks after their affairs, sells for them, and looks after them, he will receive his reward from Allah.’ I then asked, ‘What do you say about one who buys from them a slave-girl to make her mother of his child.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful if their guardian sells her for them who supervises for them in matters of their interest and they cannot revoke what the guardian has done to protect their interest.’”
